exposure: erinacine A-enriched Hericium erinaceus (EAHE) mycelia (single dose 5000 mg/kg; pregnant rats received 875, 1750, or 2625 mg/kg body weight)
outcome: death or treatment-related signs of toxicity
cohort: The study included ten Sprague-Dawley rats of both sexes for acute toxicity tests and 66 pregnant Sprague-Dawley rats for prenatal developmental toxicity tests.
finding: EAHE mycelia was considered safe and practically nontoxic for consumption within the appropriate doses and investigation period, showing no significant acute or prenatal developmental toxicity.
followup_time: 14 days for acute toxicity test; fetuses were examined on the 20th day of pregnancy.
birth_weight: Fetal body weight was measured as an outcome, but no specific inclusion criteria based on birth weight were stated.
gest_age: Fetuses were examined on the 20th day of pregnancy (rat gestation).
